title: Tracing the Winding Line

patient.name: Mdm Saraswathy d/o Pillai
patient.presenting_complaint: Colour vision check requested; she cannot read numbers, so the usual number plates cannot be used

history.hpc: Mdm Saraswathy is sent for a colour vision check. She did not have formal schooling and cannot read numbers. Her daughter says: 'My mother cannot read the number, but she can follow the line with her finger.' The PSA must adapt by using the winding-line (tracing) Ishihara plates instead of the number plates and document the result.
history.social_hx: Lives with daughter; speaks Tamil. Did not attend formal schooling.

investigations.colour_vision_ishihara: The standard number Ishihara plates are unsuitable as the patient cannot read numbers. The winding-line (tracing) plates are used instead — the patient traces the coloured line with a finger or brush. Good lighting ensured, each eye tested separately, no coaching. The result is documented (lines traced correctly).

diagnosis: Colour vision screening adapted with the winding-line (tracing) Ishihara plates for a patient who cannot read numbers. The PSA competency is recognising the need to adapt the test method, administering it correctly per eye, and documenting the result; interpretation/certification is the doctor's where needed.

immediate: Recognise that number plates are unsuitable and select the winding-line (tracing) Ishihara plates
Use the daughter to explain/demonstrate tracing the line with a finger
Ensure good, consistent lighting and that no tinted lenses are worn
Test each eye separately, allow only a few seconds per plate, and avoid coaching
Document the lines traced correctly for each eye
Report the documented result for review/certification as needed
follow_up: Provide the documented result for the requesting purpose
If results suggest a deficiency, refer for fuller assessment and doctor interpretation
File the result in the record
patient_education: Explain (via the daughter) that she only needs to trace the coloured line, not read numbers
Reassure her the test is quick and painless
Explain the result will be documented and reviewed if needed
Thank her and the daughter for their cooperation

key_points: Establishes that the patient cannot read numbers
Confirms the purpose of the colour vision check
Selects the winding-line (tracing) plates instead of number plates
Ensures good lighting and no tinted lenses
Tests each eye separately and avoids coaching
Documents lines traced correctly per eye
Recognises the need to adapt the test for a non-reader
Understands the Ishihara test screens for colour deficiency
Knows a poor result needs further assessment
Defers interpretation/certification to the doctor where needed
Administers the tracing plates correctly per eye
Refers appropriately if the result is abnormal
